From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>

Subject: NovusPay: service review and remediation log

Sarah / NovusPay ops team,

Thanks again for the call earlier — I wanted to follow up with a concise recap of what happened, the immediate mitigations we applied, and our next steps. We’ll attach a short RCA PDF and the full event timeline for your records (see attachments).

Summary (TL;DR):
- Impact: Intermittent increased latency for model streaming calls that caused token-delivery delays for a ~26-minute window on 2027-05-10 between 08:21 and 08:47 PT. No data exfiltration or model corruption detected.
- Root cause (short): A combination of an autoscaler regression (bad rolling upgrade) and a KV cache eviction storm that amplified latency under your traffic pattern.
- Customer impact: Elevated tail latency (p95->p99) and a small percentage (~0.9%) of requests hit the per-request timeout and were retried by your client.

What we did immediately:
- Rolled back the autoscaler change to the previous stable config (08:28 PT).
- Increased ephemeral cache capacity and enforced a conservative eviction policy to stop repeated cache thrashing (08:35 PT).
- Enabled a temporary routing fallback to a lower-concurrency pool to reduce queueing (08:38 PT).

Requested next steps / asks from NovusPay:
- Please confirm if you want us to provision a short-lived dedicated pool for your critical endpoints during your peak period next week.
- If you can share any client retry logs (times of the re-tried requests) we’ll correlate and quantify affected transactions.

I’ve attached the complete timeline and a concise RCA summary. I’m available to do a 30-minute walkthrough tomorrow if that’s helpful — propose 10:00 or 14:00 PT.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.com

Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>

Subject: NovusPay: consolidated RCA, timeline, and remediation log (final)

Sarah — thanks for the call earlier and for your patience while we completed the write-up. Attached is the finalized RCA (novuspay_rca_summary_20270511.pdf) plus the raw timeline CSV (novuspay_timeline_20270511.csv). Below is the consolidated customer-facing summary we reviewed on the call.

Executive summary:
- Incident window: 2027-05-10 08:21–08:47 PT (26 minutes)
- Customer-visible effect: increased streaming latency that elevated token delivery times and produced ~0.9% request timeouts (measured across your production routes). No customer data access or model output corruption observed.

Root cause (detailed):
1) Deployment regression: an autoscaler change deployed at 07:58 PT introduced a new scale-down heuristic which, under NovusPay's steady high-concurrency traffic pattern, caused more frequent pod termination and replacement events. These terminations temporarily increased request queuing.
2) KV cache eviction storm: concurrently, an aggressive eviction threshold in our in-memory KV cache caused a cascade of cache misses; the consequent rebuilds increased memory pressure and delayed streaming token assembly.
3) Amplification: the combination caused a short window where latency amplified non-linearly (small increase in queueing -> cache rebuilds -> more queueing).

Timeline (high level):
- 07:58 PT — autoscaler config change rolled (internal deploy).
- 08:21 PT — first elevated p99 observed on NovusPay routes.
- 08:28 PT — identified correlation between reduced pod count and NovusPay p99 spike; rollback of autoscaler change initiated.
- 08:35 PT — applied conservative KV cache policy and increased ephemeral cache cap.
- 08:38 PT — traffic routed to lower-concurrency fallback pool; p99 returned to baseline by 08:45 PT.
- 08:47 PT — normal routing restored.

Remediation and timeline for fixes:
- Immediate (completed): rollback + KV policy and fallback routing (done 2027-05-10).
- Short term (1–2 weeks): pin NovusPay critical routes to a dedicated small pool during peak windows; add per-account pre-warm heuristics.
- Medium term (4–8 weeks): add autoscaler canary gating and improved eviction heuristics; introduce more granular telemetry for cache churn per-account.

SLA credits and next steps:
- We’ll quantify affected requests and share the packet with you by EOD tomorrow to start the formal SLA credit review. Please copy Samantha from CS (samantha@redwood.com) on any credit requests; she will open the credit request ticket.
